chapter_seo_title: Immortal Fortunes Assembly Bloodbath Begins – 109,000 Enter the Brightmoon Painting
chapter_meta_description: The Immortal Fortunes Assembly kicks off with 109,000 geniuses thrown into the Brightmoon Landscape Painting. Only 96 can survive. Ji Ning draws his swords as the slaughter begins.
og_title: 109,000 Geniuses Enter a Killer Painting – The Immortal Fortunes Assembly Starts Now
og_description: The Grand Xia Emperor drops over a hundred thousand Wanxiang Adepts into a Pure Yang treasure world for a one-year battle royale. The rules are simple: kill for tokens or die trying.
twitter_title: The Trial of 109,000: Enter the Brightmoon Painting
twitter_description: Over 109,000 genius cultivators enter the Grand Xia Emperor's painting. Only 96 can leave alive. Ji Ning is ready.

lore_anchors.definition: The highest tier of magic treasure in the Desolate Era hierarchy, capable of containing entire worlds and possessing sentience. The Grand Xia Emperor's Brightmoon Landscape Painting is one such artifact.

A Pure Yang treasure belonging to the Grand Xia Emperor that houses a complete pocket world with mountains, rivers, and a moon; used as the arena for the first trial of the Immortal Fortunes Assembly.
A measurable cosmic 'bank account' of good deeds; cultivators with high karmic merit literally radiate golden light and are blessed with increased luck.
An invisible blessing from fortune, lineage, or encounters with great powers; distinct from karmic merit and much harder to judge.
A cultivator at the fourth major Ki Refining realm, meaning 'Myriad Manifestations,' whose Violet Palace contains stars, moon, and sun, granting vastly increased energy absorption.
A jade token distributed to each participant in the Brightmoon Landscape Painting trial; discarding it equates to surrender and immediate teleportation out of the trial.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the Brightmoon Landscape Painting?
cultural_notes_faq.a: A Pure Yang magic treasure owned by the Grand Xia Emperor that contains an entire world; it's used as the arena for the first trial of the Immortal Fortunes Assembly.

cultural_notes_faq.q: How many can pass the first trial?
cultural_notes_faq.a: A minimum of 80 and a maximum of 96 participants will survive the Brightmoon Landscape Painting trial, selected by the number of talisman-tokens they collect.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why are talismans and puppets banned?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The Emperor wants to test the participants' true personal strength and comprehension of the Dao, not their stash of external gadgets.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the difference between karmic merit and luck?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Karmic merit comes from doing good deeds and is visible as golden light; luck is an invisible blessing from one's lineage, encounters, or powerful connections.
